rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 7-8 and Table F.3 - the paper, though mostly a survey, reports its own experiment: a fine-tuned VGG16 with a new fully connected layer and Adam optimiser trained on a Mendeley tomato-pest image dataset (4263 images, 8 pest classes), reaching about 96.5% test accuracy versus SGD, RMSProp, Adam and plain VGG16 variants.
rows.notes: The study's only own result is image-based classification of eight tomato pests from ground-level photographs (Sections 7-8, Figs 12-19, Table F.3). It reports nothing of its own on remote sensing, weed detection, herbicide application, herbicide reduction or environmental effect. The weed-detection and herbicide-spraying material in Section 2.3 (Yu et al. 2019, Bah et al. 2018, Huang et al. 2020) and the statements about precise spraying reducing herbicides are cited or asserted, not the authors' own findings. The claim is therefore unsupported by the study's own evidence: pest detection is at most a precondition of targeted chemical application (upstream), and the technology (ground image classification of pests) differs from the remote sensing of weeds named in the passage.

notes: The document is a hybrid survey plus a proposed deep-learning pest-detection model. Only the model experiment (Sections 7-8) counts as own data; all weed, herbicide, UAV and remote-sensing content is review material citing other work. Text appears complete.
